explanation: The prophet and leader who led the Israelites out of Egypt and received the Ten Commandments from God.
A holy day of rest to be kept weekly, where no work is to be done but time is to be used to honor God.
A special place dedicated to God's worship and presence, often a temple or tabernacle.
Gifts or donations given voluntarily for a specific cause, in this case the building of the holy place.
People with special skills in art, design, and construction who work on making materials and objects.
A chest made of acacia wood and gold that contained the Ten Commandments, also known as the Ark of the Testimony.
The supreme religious leader responsible for performing the most important ceremonies and rituals in the holy place.
